title: [recoverability] The page says how old the newest cloud backups are: the database copy and the bundle of transcripts and sources
prompt:
Read crates/spawn-cli/src/serve.rs (`fleet()` and its `health` object), crates/spawn-postgres's backup records (`backup_records`, the `backup.dumped` and `backup.bundled` control records spawn_backup_record writes, with `keys` and `bytes`), crates/spawn-cli/src/alerts.rs (`backup_stale`) and web/src/resources.ts (the storage card's model).

The problem (owner, 2026-11-12 13:30; sync/roadmap-effects.md, "North-star and guardrail metrics", Recoverability). The age of the newest cloud backup is a recoverability guardrail, and no figure says it ("Not read today; to be collected"). The record has it: every upload is a `backup.dumped` (the database, hourly) or a `backup.bundled` (transcripts and sources, daily), with its time, its keys and its bytes. The alert step reads them for `backup_stale` (a dump older than 2 h, a bundle older than 26 h), but no answer carries them, so the page cannot show how old the copies are until one is already late.

Required behaviour.
(a) `GET /api/fleet`'s `health.backups` is {dump, bundle}: each the newest record of its kind, as {at_ms, key, bytes} (`key` the record's first uploaded key, `bytes` its bytes), or null when there is none.
(b) web/src/resources.ts exports `backupView(backups, now)`: rows [{name, age_ms, key}], "Database copy" (the dump) then "Transcripts and sources" (the bundle), `age_ms` being now less the record's at_ms. A kind with no record is a row with age_ms null and key null. The module keeps loading with node alone.
(c) The storage card on the page shows the two rows: the name, the age said as a span ("32 min", "10 h"), and "no backup yet" for a null age. Read off a screenshot.

Ranges, for the core-lines card that comes later and not for this objective: the cloud backup guardrail is a dump at most 2 h old and a bundle at most 26 h old, the same as backup_stale. A 24 h bundle range would flap every day, since the daily bundle lands a little more than 24 h after the one before.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/082.sh. The history is seeded as the store holds it, as control records hours before one fixed "now", and `spawn serve` answers. Dumps at -1.5 h and -0.5 h, one bundle at -10 h. Checks:
- (1) through `GET /api/fleet`: health.backups.dump is the -0.5 h dump {at_ms, key "postgres/hourly/spawn-bb-2.dump.gpg", bytes 9400000}, and health.backups.bundle is the bundle {at_ms, key "bundles/incr/spawn-bundle-bb-1.tar.zst.gpg", bytes 5000000};
- (2) under node, backupView over that answer gives Database copy at 30 min and Transcripts and sources at 10 h with their keys, and a null bundle gives the row {name "Transcripts and sources", age_ms null, key null}.
It fails with 1 on b4cda42e: /api/fleet has no health.backups, and resources.ts has no backupView.

The product reason. Recoverability is the line about surviving a loss, and the owner can only trust it by seeing that the off-host copies are fresh. Today the first sign of a stopped backup is the backup_stale alert, hours after the copies stopped. Monitoring only: no gate, integrator or deploy step reads it.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/, web/test/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base, any lint relaxation and any build-time code. The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host. Keep every existing check green (040, 043, 045, 046, 047, 049, 065 and 074 read /api/fleet) and add tests of your own for the new behaviour: a serve test of health.backups (newest of each kind, null when none), and a web/test test of backupView.
